Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business

boom noun

a time of growing trade and wealth

also economic boom, booming, prosperity, prosper, thrive, flourish, be booming

classical

Cic. Inv. 2.1: omnibus cōpiīs, of Croton in its prime (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 1.1 (Lewis & Short)

flōreō, flōrēre, flōruī

verb, second conjugation

flourish, prosper, boom

To be in flower, and so to be at the height of prosperity or fame: of cities, peoples, trades and men (rēs flōrent, business is booming). Latin says the thing booms rather than naming “a boom”.

Other words

  • prosperitās, prosperitātis f. — prosperity, good fortune

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 3.86: vītae (Lewis & Short); Nep. Att. 21.1 (Lewis & Short)

    Rare but good prose (Lewis & Short); good fortune in general, not trade alone. The common phrase is rēs secundae, prosperity.

Examples

  • Mercātūra hōc annō flōret.

    Trade is booming this year.composed

See also economy, rich, increase, business.

SourcesLewis & Short: floreo · Lewis & Short: prosperitas
